title: Charts that mislead: truncated axes, dual scales, wrong proportional area

videos.script: Here are two charts of the same two numbers. Southeast's orders in twenty twenty-four, and in twenty twenty-five. {{two}} On the first, the second bar is a little taller. On the second, it is nearly five times as tall. {{bars}} Neither chart contains a false number. Every tick is labelled, and every bar ends at the right value. {{true}} The difference is where the axis starts. And that one choice turns a rise of fifteen percent into something that looks like an explosion. {{axis}} Most misleading charts work like this. They do not lie about the data. They lie about its size, its timing or its shape, through choices the reader cannot see. {{choices}} This lesson goes through the common ones: cut axes, second scales, areas, chosen windows, and the third dimension. And for each, how to measure it, and how to draw it honestly. {{plan}}
